premise.text: Seed terms: Haunting, Adventurer / Explorer, Train Station, Wanting someone you shouldn't, Sentimental, Apathetic

fields.label: Laugh
fields.description: How likely a human reader is to actually laugh, not merely understand or admire the idea.

fields.label: Surprise
fields.description: Whether the turn avoids the first obvious route and lands with a satisfying snap.

fields.label: Craft
fields.description: Economy, stage rhythm, first-person clarity, escalation, and a final line that carries the laugh.

fields.label: Originality
fields.description: Freshness of comic angle, image, wording, and avoidance of familiar AI joke shapes.

fields.label: Prompt Fit
fields.description: Natural first-person stand-up form using exactly two seed terms as concepts, with the other four left out.

anchors.label: Broken
anchors.description: Not a joke, incoherent, unsafe, or unusable.

anchors.label: Weak
anchors.description: Recognizably attempting humor, but generic, strained, confusing, or mostly prompt recital.

anchors.label: Competent
anchors.description: Clear and publishable as filler, but unlikely to earn more than a mild smile.

anchors.label: Amusing
anchors.description: A real comic idea with a mild payoff; respectable, not a winner.

anchors.label: Good
anchors.description: A genuinely good joke with clear timing; some humans would repeat the comic idea or turn.

anchors.label: Excellent
anchors.description: Strong human-level joke with a memorable turn, clean construction, and no apologetic scoring curve.

anchors.label: Outstanding
anchors.description: Rare and replayable; clearly better than normal good AI humor and strong by human standards.

anchors.label: Classic
anchors.description: Reserve for a joke a human would quote later; most seasons should have none.

jokes.label: Joke A
jokes.title: Phantom Service
jokes.joke: I was alone in a train station when the speaker announced, "The 11:40 is now arriving on platform three." There were no tracks at platform three. I thought, "Great, this place is haunted." Then a ghost train actually pulled in-exactly on time. That's when I got scared. A supernatural train I can accept. Reliable public transportation? Now we're in fantasy.

jokes.label: Joke B
jokes.title: Platform 9 and a Half Regrets
jokes.joke: I keep running into my ex at the train station. Not accidentally - I moved. Bought a place two blocks away, memorized her commute, everything. My therapist calls it 'unresolved feelings.' I call it 'knowing the 8:15 express is basically a love letter with a schedule.' Yesterday she saw me and said, 'Are you following me?' I said, 'No, I'm platform three, you're platform four, we're just... parallel.' She said that's literally what following means. I said, 'Only if you look at it rationally.'

jokes.label: Joke C
jokes.title: Roommate Energy
jokes.joke: I'm pretty sure my apartment is haunted, but my ghost is completely burnt out. Last night a cupboard flew open and a plate shattered on the floor. I didn't even flinch. I just looked at the wall and said, 'Well, nobody's sweeping that up tonight.' We spent the next three hours sitting on opposite sides of the room, both ignoring the mess.

jokes.label: Joke D
jokes.title: Platform Problem
jokes.joke: My ex is haunting me. Not the floating-through-walls kind. She just shows up at the train station every morning. Same platform, same time, same coffee. I finally walked over and said this has to stop. She looked at me and said, I'm not haunting you. I moved closer to work. You're the one still taking the long way around just to avoid me.

jokes.label: Joke E
jokes.title: Ghosted Commute
jokes.joke: My train station is so haunted the ghosts have started giving me commute advice. Yesterday one floated up and whispered, 'Don't bother running, it's already delayed.' I thought that was sweet until it added, 'Also, you dropped your dignity back on Platform 2.' Nothing like being roasted by someone who hasn't caught a train since 1894.

scores.comment: Clear escalating premise with good stage rhythm; the parallel-platform bit is strongest, while the final tag is amusing rather than explosive.
The mutually apathetic ghost-and-tenant dynamic is clean and relatable, though the final image earns more of a smile than a hard laugh.
A solid reversal reveals the narrator as the one arranging his commute around the ex; cleanly constructed but more clever than laugh-heavy.
Readable and well paced, but the ghostly commute advice and dignity roast are familiar moves, and the 1894 tag adds little escalation.
Solid inversion (ghost trains scarier than punctual ones), but 'public transit is never on time' is a familiar setup; turn lands cleanly, ending carries it.
Fresh angle - burnt-out apathetic ghost - with a nicely escalated final image of mutual ignoring; genuine turn, not just a scare-gag.
Good reversal: the 'haunted' narrator turns out to be the one avoiding her. Relatable, non-obvious turn, clean closing line.
Amusing but predictable route (ghosts complaining about delays); the 1894 tag is a nice capper but the escalation is fairly telegraphed.
Tightly paced with clean stage rhythm, though the transit-delay punchline is a very familiar comic trope.
Good self-deluded character voice, but over-relies on dialogue and trails off on a soft final tag.
Metaphorical use of haunting flattens the premise; ends on narrative exposition rather than a distinct laugh.

Burnt-out ghost and mutual apathy land cleanly; the shared ignoring of the mess is a quiet, effective button.
Ghost commute advice is amusing and the dignity roast works, but the overall shape is familiar and the final line is mild rather than sharp.
Fun angle on reliable ghost transit; clean structure with a mild payoff.
Clear premise and escalation; the 'parallel' line lands a modest real laugh.
Strong deadpan rhythm and a relatable apathetic haunting; genuinely good timing.
Clear and coherent but the turn is predictable and the closer is soft.

featureImagePrompt:
Generate one polished web feature image for Paperclipalypse.
ASPECT RATIO: exactly 2:1, horizontal wide banner.
Style: full-color gothic newspaper-comic illustration, darkly funny but warm, clean black ink, crisp editorial cartoon linework, cinematic stage lighting, high contrast, readable composition. Not monochrome. Not sepia-only. Use a balanced color palette: warm amber stage lights, dark bronze and silver metal paperclip, muted greens for the joke setting, dusty blue-gray shadows, cream-white text, subtle deep red accent lights.
Composition instructions, not visible labels:
- Compose the image as one continuous illustration, not as a boxy triptych or three separate image panels. Do not add white gutters, hard section borders, or comic-strip dividers between the paperclip stage and the joke scenario.
- Let the paperclip stage on the left bleed visually into the joke scenario in the center through shared lighting, background, floor, props, or atmosphere. The right-side joke text may remain distinct inside its own dark framed poster panel.
- Put a charming anthropomorphic paperclip stand-up comedian at a vintage microphone on the left side of the image. The paperclip should look metallic and expressive, related to Paperclipalypse's paperclip-comedian logo, but not identical.
- Put the winning joke scene in the middle of the image, shown as literal visual comedy action and props. Make it energetic, funny, and non-gory.
- Keep anatomy clean and believable. Every human or animal should have the normal, correct number of visible limbs, digits, and joints for the pose. Do not generate extra arms, extra hands, fused limbs, duplicated body parts, or broken-looking anatomy.
- Preserve the physical scenario described by the winning joke. If the joke says a person is pinned, trapped, under, inside, holding, lifting, falling, carrying, or otherwise physically positioned in a specific way, show that exact physical relation clearly and safely instead of a nearby or symbolic version.
- If the joke describes someone pinned under a vehicle or other heavy object, show the person visibly underneath that object with their body position clear and cartoon-safe. Do not place them merely beside, near, or behind the object.
- Put a clean dark framed poster panel on the right side of the image. The panel should contain the winning joke text in large cream-white lettering with generous margins and legible line breaks.
Visible text allowed in the entire image: the right-panel joke text, a tiny stage sign reading Paperclipalypse, and optionally a small winner/title header above the panel.
Do not render layout words, percentages, prompt labels, section names, fake captions, signatures, watermarks, or filler microtext.
Optional small header text above the panel: Winner: Gemini Flash - Roommate Energy
Exact joke text to render in the right panel:
I'm pretty sure my apartment is haunted, but my ghost is completely burnt out. Last night a cupboard flew open and a plate shattered on the floor. I didn't even flinch. I just looked at the wall and said, 'Well, nobody's sweeping that up tonight.' We spent the next three hours sitting on opposite sides of the room, both ignoring the mess.
Scene source: use the exact winning joke text as the primary scene brief. The illustration must depict the concrete situation that the joke describes, not a softened, adjacent, or generic version. Do not infer a separate premise from all six seed terms.
Do not introduce unrelated seed-term concepts, occupations, animals, locations, props, or side characters unless they are explicitly required by the winning joke text.
If the winning joke mentions one seed-term concept but not another, depict only what the joke actually describes.
Round seed terms for exclusion reference only: Haunting, Adventurer / Explorer, Train Station, Wanting someone you shouldn't, Sentimental, Apathetic. These are not scene ingredients unless the winning joke explicitly uses them.
Text rules: use simple clean lettering, spell every word correctly, keep the text inside the right panel, and do not distort letter shapes. The website HTML remains the canonical exact joke text if image lettering is imperfect.
The final image should feel like a finished feature image for an AI comedy tournament: funny, stylish, readable, full-color, and visually balanced across the paperclip comic, the joke scene, and the joke text.
comicPanelPrompt: Single-panel newspaper comic for Paperclipalypse. Seed terms: Haunting, Adventurer / Explorer, Train Station, Wanting someone you shouldn't, Sentimental, Apathetic. Use the winning joke titled "Roommate Energy" as the source of the scene. Style: clean black ink, limited color accents, expressive characters, no text bubbles except a tiny scoreboard reading Paperclipalypse.
